Fazlul Huq Khan Farid with Mostafa Zaman Islam, Advocates ----- For the Appellant.
Umme Kulsum Begum; Deputy Attorney-General with SM Shajahan Kabir, Assistant Attorney-General ----- For the State-Respondent.
parties:
Pashan Ali ----- Appellant 
Vs.
State ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This Criminal Appeal under section 24 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 is directed against the judgment and order dated 25-9-2002 passed by the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishes Adalat No. 2, Gaibandha, in Nari-o- Shishu Nirjatan Daman case No. 83 of 1999 arising out of GR Case No. 128 of 1999 (Fulchari) corresponding to Fulchari PS Case No. 7 dated 29-1-1999 convicting the appellant under section 9(Kha) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman (Bis-hesh Bidhan) Ain, 1999 and convicting him there under to suffer imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Taka 10,000 in default to suffer imprisonment for 2(two) years more.

2. The prosecution case, in short, is that, on 29-1-1999 one Md Ekhlesuddin as informant lodged a first information report against the appellant and another accused person under section 9(kha)(Ga)/14 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 alleging, inter alia, that on the night following 25-1-1999 at 4-30 AM appellant and two others entered into the room by breaking the door and abducted his daughter Jesmin fastening her face; that witnesses namely Anisa and Bittu who tried to resist but they were threatened and assaulted by the accused persons and that the witnesses recognised accused Pashan by the light of burning hurricane. It is further stated that at the time of occurrence he was staying at Rangpur and that returning from Rangpur, he being informed came to know about the alleged occurrence. Hence the first information report.

3. SI Md Shajahan, investigated the case. During investigation, he visited the place of occurrence, prepared sketch map of the place of occurrence with separate index thereof, seized hurricane as alamat through seizure list and kept the same in the jimma of PW 1 informant. He tried to secure arrest of accused but he could not do so as he was absconding then. He recorded the statements of I witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and finding prima facie case submitted charge sheet being No, 28 dated 30-4-1999 against accused Pashan Ali and Nura Sheikh under section 9(kba)(ga)/14 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995.

4. The learned trial Court framed charge under section 9(kha) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 against accused Pashan Ali and the Charges were read over to the accused in open Court in which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried as per law.

5. Accused Nura Sheikh was discharged from charge under section 9(kha)/14 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 as no element for framing charge was available against him.

6. The prosecution examined 6 (six) PWs. After examination of PWs, accused was examined under section 34i of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the accused pleaded not guilty and filed papers and declined to examine any witness on his behalf,

7. The defence case as it transpires from the trend of cross-examination and the suggestions put forward to the witnesses is that accused Pashan Ali did not kidnap victim Jasmin and she voluntarily went to him as she fell in love with him and that the informant lodged a false case against him as he could not accept their marriage.

8. Thereafter on consideration of the evidence on record as well as the facts and circumstances of the case, the learned, Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Adalat No. 2, Gaibandha, found the accused Pashan Ali guilty under section 9(kha) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 1995 and convicted him thereunder to suffer imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Taka 10,000 in default to suffer imprisonment for 4(two) years more.

9. The accused appellant, being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order of conviction under section 9(kha) of the Nari for Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 1999 has come up with the present appeal which is, opposed by the respondent State through learned Deputy Attorney General.

10. Mr Fazlul Huq Khan Farid with Mr Mostafa Zaman Islam, the learned Advocate for the. appellant, took us to the first information report, the charge so framed, the deposition of the prosecution witnesses, impugned judgment and the material papers and documents which are available in the paper books and submits that the victim Jesmin fell in love with accused Pashan Ali, that she voluntarily went to him and that the informant lodged the false case against him as he could not accept their marriage. He further submits that the learned trial Court arrived at a decision basing on conjectures and surmises; that the learned trial Court failed to consider the prosecution case and that all the prosecution witnesses are interested and tutored witnesses and their evidence has not been corroborated by any independent witnesses. He further submits that the learned Judge failed to scrutinise the evidence of witnesses in proper perspective since they are interested witnesses and the learned Court failed to apply his judicial mind assessing the evidence and that the impugned judgment is illegal and unwarranted by facts and circumstances of the case, as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside.

11. Mr Umme Kulsum Begum, the learned Deputy Attorney-General with Mr SM Shajahan Kabir, the learned Assistant Attorney-General for the State, on the other hand, submit that, the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Adalat No. 2, Gaibandha, was justified in convicting and sentencing accused appellant Pashan Ali assessing the evidence on record. She further submits that the prosecution has proved its case against the accused by most consistent, corroborative and overwhelming evidence; that the learned Judge was perfectly justified in convicting and sentencing the accused appellant on the basis of the most cogent and reliable evidence and that his judgment does not suffer from any misreading and non-reading of evidence. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that all the prosecution witnesses are natural, probable and competent witnesses and there is no internal points of falsehood in their evidence on any point and, as such, the impugned judgment calls for no interference by the Court.

12. The only point for determination in the appeal is, whether the learned Judge was justified in convicting and sentencing accused appellant Pashan Ali under section 9(kha) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 1995.

13. In the face of arguments advanced by the learned Advocates of the contending parties, we are now called upon to scrutinise material evidence on record to come to proper decision in this appeal.

14. PW 1, Md Ekhles Uddin is the father of the victim Jesmin who deposed that persons entered into the living room of his daughter Jesmin on 25-1-1999 at 4-00 AM; that his 'Bhagni' Anisa was also sleeping in her room; that Anisa woke up hearing the sound of struggle and found the mouth. of his daughter tied up; that bhagni could recognise the accused Pashan Ali out of three; that Pashan Ali kicked on the chest and belly of Anisa and also inflicted fist blow; that she would not say anything; that his minor son Bittu and daughter Anjuara tried to go to that room hearing the sound; that Bittu saw that three persons were dragging her out through the door; that Pashan Ali shown him arms and kicked him and told that he would be finished if he would say anything and he could recognise the accused Pashan Ali with the help of light of burning hurricane in the room and that they have taken away Jesmin by force. This witness further stated that his daughter was kidnapped for marriage and he also heard that Pashan Ali married his daughter taking her to the district Panchagraharh, PW 1 further stated that Pashan Ali brought her in his house back on 28-3-2000 and killed her in his house under his custody as Jesmin expressed her unwillingness to tell before the Court what were already tutored to her.

15. PW 2, Bittu Miah, stated that when he was sleeping in his room besides the room of Jesmin, he heard sound of struggle on 25-1-1999 at 4-30 AM, then he woke up and saw that mouth of Jesmin was tied up and three miscreants were dragging Jesmin out of the room. He could recognise one Pashan Ali with the help of light of burning hurricane; that when he went to oppose but he was kicked and then he raised alarm but the miscreants threatened him on dagger's point saying that he would be finished if he would raise alarm, after that incident he did not see Jesmin alive. He went to the house of younger brother of Pashan Ali after 13 months after she was killed and found many injuries in her body including neck. He further stated that he heard that she was killed when she did not agree to tell before Court what was tutored to her.

16. PW 3, Anju Ara, deposed that she was sleeping in the room besides the room of Jesmin; that she heard the sound of struggle from the room of Jesmin at about 4-30 AM and then she entered into that room, that she saw her mouth tied up; that she also saw 3 persons in that room; that she could recognise Pashan Ali with the light of hurricane; that Pashan threatened her on arms pointsaying that she would not shout; that they took Jesmin away and she searched for Jesmin in the house of Pashan Ali but failed.

17. PW 4,Anisa Khatun alias Anju Ara, deposed that she was sleeping in the same bed of Jesmin after her finishing studies lit night on 25-1- 999; that she woke up 4-30 AM after hearing some sounds in the room and saw the mouth of Jesmin being tied that she saw three persons in the room and that she could recognise Pashan Ali with the light of burning hurricane on the table. When she was about to shout, then accused Pashan Ali stopped her shouting on arms point and that they took her away by force. Pashan Ali gave her fist blow on her chest; that she became senseless and that, Jesmiri thereafter could not be found even after search. She further stated that she saw the dead body of Jesmin in the house of younger brother of Pashan after 13 months; that she saw injuries in her body and that she further heard that Pashan Ali killed her when she did not agree to tell before the Court the matter already tutored to her.

PW 5 Mst Nol Begum deposed that she was sleeping in a room beside the room of Jesmin; that she woke up hearing sound of struggle in the room of Jesmin: that Anisa and she went to that room and saw Jesmin's mouth was being tied. It is further stated that when she raised alarm accused Pashan Ali threatened her on arms point and that Pashan Ali took Jesmin away by force. She could recognise Pashan with the help of light of burning hurricane on the table.

18. PW 6 Mohammad Shajahan, investigating  officer, testified that; informant Ekhlesuddin Sarker stated in his ejhar that accused Pashan Ali and 2 unknown persons kidnapped his daughter on 25-1-1999 at about 4-30 AM. During investigation he visited the place of occurrence, prepared sketch map with index thereof, seized hurricane as alamat and gave the same in the jimma of the informant, recorded statement of witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and that he tried to secure arrest of the accused Pashan Ali but could not secure arrest because of absconsion and could not recover the victim as the accused was absconding.

19. These are all the evidence produced by the prosecution.

20. The allegation against the accused Pashan, Ali is that he with the help of others abducted the me victim Jesmin for the purpose of marrying her for which he was convicted under section 9(Kha) of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995.

21. The defence case is that Jesmin loveed Pashan Ali and out of that love, she voluntarily went her to Pashan and married him having registered Kabinnama.

22. The fundamental and basic presumption in the administration of criminal law and justice delivery system is that the accused should be presumed to be innocent till the charges are proved beyond reasonable doubt on the basis of clear, cogent, credible unimpeachable evidence. In a criminal trial, the burden of proving guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt always rests on the prosecution and on its failure, it cannot fall back upon the accused. In a criminal case, it is for, the on prosecution to bring the guilt home to the accused.

<u>23. In the instant case the prosecution has taken alibi that the victim Jesmin loved Pashan Ali and she went to him and married him having registered kabinnama. When the accused has taken the plea of alibi, in such case the burden of proof lies on the appellant who substantially asserts that the victim Jesmin loved him and she went with him voluntarily. It is also decided in case of Soma Bhai vs State of Gujarat reported in 1975 SC 1453 that the plea of alibi has got to be proved by the defence to the satisfaction of the Court. It is stated in the case of State of Maharashtra vs Narsingarao Gangaram Pimple reported 1 CrLJ 1984 that the plea of alibi must be proved with absolute certainty.</u>

24. Now let us see how far the respective parties have succeeded in proving their respective burden.

25. The background of this case is that after taking away the victim Jesmin by accused Pashan Ali he married her and kept her in his custody for about 13 months and thereafter the victim Jesmin died. The prosecution alleged that accused Pashan Ali killed her while she was under his custody, on the other hand the defence version that the victim committed suicide taking poison. Another case was filed against the accused Pashan Ali for committing murder of victim Jesmin. But the evidence on record shows that the accused Pashan Ali has other two wives. Defence submitted some documents including alleged kabinnama. It appears from alleged Kabinnama of victim Jesmin that kabinnama was registered giving false particulars. Column 21 of the Kabinnama shows that first wife of accused Pashan Ali was dead but the certificate granted by the Chairman shows that the first wife was alive. Thus it appears that the defence version is not fair.

26. Section 9(kha) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) is that whoever, by force takes away any woman against her will and compelled her to marry him, shall be punished of either description with imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprison, ment for 10 years which shall not be imprisonment for 7 years and shall also liable to fine.

27. The moot question that calls for our determination is, whether the victim Jesmin went with the accused Pashan Ali out of love or she was taken away against her will and whether she was compelled to marry him.

28. As per the provision of law stated herein- before respective party is to prove its part,

29. The prosecution has examined 6 PWs in support of his contention.

30. PW 1 Md Ekhlesuddin is the informant of the case who is also the father of the victim Jesmin, He corroborating the first information report case deposed that the accused Pashan Ali and two other unknown persons kidnapped his daughter Jesmin Akhter from her living room on 25-1-1999 at about 4-30 AM; that the witnesses Bittu, Anisa and Anjuara witnessed the occurrence. PW 2 Bittu is the son of informant, PW 3 Anjuara is the daughter of the informant, PW 4 Anisa Khatun is the cousin sister of the victim Jesmin and PW 5 Nol Begum is the grandmother of the victim, PW 2 Bittu, PW 3 Anjuara and PW 5 Nol Begum were sleeping in the adjacent room which was by the side of the victim's room.

31. PWs 2 to 5 chorusly deposed that while accused Pashan Ali and other unknown persons were kidnapping, they opposed but accused Pashan Ali threatened them with dire consequence of death if they would shout and oppose. They all sustained blows, even Anisa PW 4 became senseless suffering the blow.

32. PW 1, informant, stated with force that his son and daughter could recognise accused Pashan Ali by the light of burning hurricane. His son and daughter were sleeping in adjacent room at the time of occurrence. Anjuara and Bittu woke up hearing sound of struggle in the room of victim. The defence has not challenged it in cross-examination. He stated in his cross-examination that his son and daughter raised hue and cry after the occurrence. He also stated that his son and daughter having been minor accused Pashan kicked them. As a result they could not shout at the time of occurrence. The question of awakening and raising of alarm also have been stated by PWs 4 to 5 in their cross-examination, As such awakening and raising of alarm has been proved. As regard the arrival of Anju Ara, Bittu and Nol Begum, there has been coming consequential evidence. PW 2 Bittu Miah, PW 3 Anju Ara and PW 4 Anisa Khatun stated in their respective examination-in-chief about what each individually lias seen at the time of occurrence.

33. PW 2 Bittu Miah stated in his cross-examination that he heard the shouting of Anju Ara. Hearing the shouting of Anjuara he went there and they both raised shouting. He Saw Anisa lying on the bed. The defence has not challenged it in their cross-examination.

34. PWs 1 to 5 chorusly deposed that accused Pashan Ali and others had taken away the victim by force. The defence has not challenged those evidence in cross examination.

35. In the face of these evidence we are led to believed that the victim was dragged out of the room where the victim was sleeping. It appears from the evidence of PWs 1 to 5 that accused Pashan Ali and two other unknown persons kidnapped Jesmin from the living room. They recognised accused Pashan Ali with the help of light of hurricane in the room. This hurricane according to Pw 6 was seized and given in the Jimma of PW 1 under Jimmanama Exhibit 6/2. There is evidence from PW 3 that accused Pashan was previously known to them, So it was possible for PWs 2 to 5 to recognise accused Pashan Ali with the help of light of burning hurricane on the table. It appears from the evidence of PW 5 that accused Pashan Ali could not be found at his house when he was searched immediately after occurrence. PW 6 Md Shajahan, the investigating officer, stated that he tried to secure arrest of accused Pashan but failed due to absconsion of the accused. Documents submitted by accused show that accused Pashan Ali was in the district of Pachagarh on 15-2-1999. There is no case of the defence that accused has not absconded in the aforesaid way or that accused Pashan was not living with Jesmin in the said district from before 25-1-1999. Thus we find that accused Pashan Ali absconded immediately after occurrence.

36. The evidence of PWs 2 to 5 are direct as eye-witnesses. Their above mentioned evidence are corroborative and consistent. We find no reason to disbelieve them.

37. The defence case is that Jesmin loved Pashan. Out of love she voluntarily went to Pashan Ali and married him having registered Kabinnama. The defence has not categorised in the cross-examination as to where and how the marriage Was solemnised. It appears from Kabinnama that kabinnama was registered giving false particulars. Column 21 of the Kibannama shows that first wife was dead but certificate granted by chairman and produced by prosecution shows that first wife was alive, If there was love and Jesmin went to Pashan Ali voluntarily then why Pashan kept her at his house and why he Would abscond soon after occurrence. Had there been any love between Pashan and Jesmin, Pashan would have been present when suratal of the dead body of Jesmin was prepared and when UD case No. 2 of 2000 was started. Again, the defence has not ventilated in Court as to when Jesmin went to Pashan voluntarily. On the other hand prosecution proved the date on 25-1-1999 at 4-30 AM for kidnapping of the victim, Jesmin. In absence of any other date and time from the side of the defence, the date of occurrence on 25-1-1999 at 4-30 AM has been taken to be proved.

38. Now let us reply the arguments raised by the defence as regard the interested and relative witnesses.

39. In the instant case PW 2 Bittu and PW 3 Anjuara are the brother and sister of the victim respectively. PW 4 Anisa is cousin sister of the victim and PW 5 Nol Begum is the grandmother of victim. It appears from the evidence that Anisa sleeping with the victim Jesmin, PW 2 Bittu and PW 3 Anjuara and PW 5 Nol Begum were sleeping in the room beside the room of the victim. Hearing the screams, they came to the room of Jesmin and recognised the accused Pashan Ali In the instant case, though they are relatives of the informant, still they are the most natural witnesses. In this circumstance of the case, the prosecution witnesses cannot be disbelieved merely on the ground of their relationship because they are eye-witnesses of the occurrence.

<u>40. In order to appreciate evidence, the Court is required to bear in mind the set up and environment in which the crime is committed and the level of understanding of the witnesses. Bearing in mind these broad principles, the evidence is required to beappreciated to find out what part out of the evidence represents the truth and correct state of affairs. It is for the Court to separate the grain from the chaff. A close relative who is natural witness cannot be regarded as an interested witness. In instant case PW 2, Bittu Miah, PW 3, Anju Ara, PW 4, Anisa Khatun, and PW 5, No-1 Begum, are the eye-witnesses and they cannot be regarded as interested witnesses and their evidence cannot be disbelieved without any rhyme and reasons. It is normally expected that a witness would not implicate an innocent man without any reason rather would connect the real culprits. Where the testimony of witnesses in whose presence the occurrence took place, their evidence cannot be discarded; that they all were close relatives of the victim. It is necessary that the testimony of interested witness must be viewed with high decree of caution and the Court should also look for independent corroboration. In the instant case, having given our anxious consideration, we can safely hold that the testimony of PWs 1 to 4 are supported by the facts and circumstances of the case. So their evidence should be accepted.</u>

41. In view of the above facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, we are of the view that there was no love affair between Jesmin and Pashan Ali and that Jesmin has not gone to Pashan voluntarily. On the other hand, prosecution has proved that Pashan Ali with two other unknown persons kidnapped Jesmin for marriage on 25-1-1999 at 4-30 AM from living room of Jesmin.

42. It appears that the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan DamanTribunal, Gaibandha, has given the highest punishment like life imprisonment embodied in section 9(kha) of the Ain, Considering age, minor children and helpless condition of his family members, term of conviction can be reduced to minimum term of 7(seven) years for ends of justice.

43. For the reasons stated above the appeal succeeded in part.

44. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part and the judgment and order dated 25-9-2002 passed by the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Adalat No. 2 Gaibandha, in Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No. 83 of 1999 is modified and his term of imprisonment is altered from imprisonment for life to imprisonment for 7 (seven) years with fine of Taka 5000 in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 1(one) year and the appellant is also entitled to get benefit of section 35A of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Send down the LCR at once.

End.
